items.title: Areas of Circles: Word Problems

sections.normalized_html: The window in the attic of Mary's house has the shape of a quarter circle, as shown below. If the area of ​​the window is [MATH: \dfrac{\pi}{2}\,\textrm{m}^2,] what is the diameter of the corresponding circle?
sections.readable_text:
The window in the attic of Mary's house has the shape of a quarter circle, as shown below. If the area of ​​the window is [MATH: \dfrac{\pi}{2}\,\textrm{m}^2,] what is the diameter of the corresponding circle?

[IMG: /graphics/481477146b092be32627f9d298229955]

sections.normalized_html:
The area of the circle is four times the area of the quarter section. So, [MATH: \mathcal{A}=4\cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} =2\pi\,\textrm{m}^2.]

The formula for the area of a circle is [MATH: \mathcal{A}=\pi r^2], where [MATH: r] is the radius. Therefore,

[MATH: A|= πr^{2}; 2π|= πr^{2}; 2π|= πr^{2}; 2|= r^{2}; r|= sqrt(2)m.]

Finally, the diameter is [MATH: d=2\cdot r= 2\cdot \sqrt{2}=2\sqrt{2}\,\textrm{m} .]
